steps.tx: An **acute myeloid leukaemia** represents a clonal hematopoietic stem cell malignancy characterized by blocked myeloid differentiation and uncontrolled proliferation. Accumulating immature myeloid precursors progressively replace normal bone marrow elements, causing severe pancytopenia. Diagnostic criteria established by the World Health Organization mandate a minimum threshold of twenty percent myeloid blast cells in the peripheral blood or bone marrow aspirate.
steps.say: Acute myeloid leukaemia is a malignant stem cell disorder where differentiation freezes at an immature blast stage. Clonal blasts crowd out the bone marrow, triggering severe anaemia, infection, and bleeding. The World Health Organization defines AML by finding at least twenty percent myeloid blasts in the blood or bone marrow.

vis.caption: Myeloblast with delicate chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and pathognomonic Auer rod.

steps.tx: The pathognomonic morphological finding is the presence of **Auer rods** within blast cytoplasm. These needle-shaped, pink-red crystalline structures represent fused, aggregated primary azurophilic granules containing abundant myeloperoxidase and lysosomal enzymes. Their identification conclusively establishes myeloid lineage, ruling out acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. Multiple stacked Auer rods, termed faggot cells, are characteristic of acute promyelocytic leukaemia.
steps.say: Auer rods are the defining microscopic hallmark of myeloid blasts. These red crystalline needles form from fused azurophilic granules packed with myeloperoxidase. Finding even a single Auer rod proves the leukaemia is myeloid and rules out ALL. Stacks of numerous Auer rods, called faggot cells, are classic in acute promyelocytic leukaemia.

vis.title: Myeloid versus Lymphoid Blast Differentiation
rows: Large (15 to 20 um) with moderate cytoplasm
Small to medium with scant cytoplasm

steps.tx: Cytochemical confirmation relies on **myeloperoxidase staining**, which produces dark brown-black cytoplasmic granulation in at least three percent of blasts. Sudan Black B parallels myeloperoxidase by staining intracellular lipids within granulocytic granules. Nonspecific esterase (alpha-naphthyl acetate esterase) staining displays intense cytoplasmic positivity in monocytic leukaemia subtypes, which is completely inhibited by the addition of sodium fluoride.
steps.say: Cytochemistry confirms myeloid identity. Myeloperoxidase staining reacts with primary granules, producing black deposits in myeloid blasts. Sudan Black B gives identical positive staining. For acute monocytic leukaemia, nonspecific esterase turns the cytoplasm bright red, and this reaction is completely blocked by adding sodium fluoride.

left.title: Granulocytic Markers
points: Sudan Black B stains granule lipids

right.title: Monocytic Markers
points: CD14 and CD64 positive by flow cytometry

steps.tx: In acute promyelocytic leukaemia (APL), the defining cytogenetic abnormality is the **PML-RARA translocation** t(15;17)(q22;q12). This reciprocal translocation fuses the PML gene on chromosome 15 to the retinoic acid receptor alpha gene on chromosome 17. The resulting chimeric oncoprotein blocks promyelocytic differentiation. These patients present with catastrophic disseminated intravascular coagulation caused by the release of procoagulant granule contents.
steps.say: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia carries the balanced translocation t(15;17), fusing PML on chromosome fifteen with RARA on chromosome seventeen. This chimeric protein arrests promyelocyte maturation. Patients frequently present with explosive disseminated intravascular coagulation from procoagulant granule release, making APL an urgent medical emergency.

vis.title: Recurrent Cytogenetic Subtypes of AML
rows: Favourable with targeted ATRA and ATO
Adverse; associated with prior topoisomerase II inhibitors

steps.tx: Targeted induction therapy for acute promyelocytic leukaemia pairs **all-trans retinoic acid** with arsenic trioxide, producing durable cures without conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy. Pharmacological concentrations of retinoic acid overcome the chimeric block, forcing malignant promyelocytes to differentiate into mature, short-lived neutrophils. Differentiation syndrome, characterized by fever, respiratory distress, and pulmonary infiltrates, is treated promptly with intravenous dexamethasone.
steps.say: Treat acute promyelocytic leukaemia with all-trans retinoic acid and arsenic trioxide. ATRA forces malignant promyelocytes to complete differentiation into mature neutrophils, curing over ninety percent of patients. Watch for differentiation syndrome, where expanding neutrophils flood the lungs with cytokines; treat it immediately with intravenous dexamethasone.

right.title: Differentiation Syndrome
points: Episodic hypotension and acute renal failure

quiz.q: Which morphological structure in blast cytoplasm conclusively confirms myeloid rather than lymphoid leukaemia?
quiz.explain: Auer rods are needle-shaped crystalline inclusions of fused azurophilic granules containing myeloperoxidase, pathognomonic of myeloblasts in AML.

quiz.q: What reciprocal chromosomal translocation defines acute promyelocytic leukaemia (AML M3)?
quiz.explain: The t(15;17)(q22;q12) translocation fuses PML on chromosome 15 with RARA on chromosome 17, creating the chimeric oncoprotein responsive to ATRA.
